feature: An empty track is drawn as the place a clip goes
summary: A track with nothing on it is now the mock's dashed, striped slot instead of bare background, so a new video shows where a clip goes before you start dragging. The slot goes when a clip lands and comes back when the last one leaves.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/empty-track-slot-walk.json.

try.do: File > New Video, press Return to keep 1920 x 1080. Look at V1 and Audio on the timeline.
Compare it with the mock's New video step 1 (video.html, New, empty).
Switch the Mac to Light appearance and look again.
File > Import Media, then drag the tile onto V1 and hold it there.
Let go, then press Command Z.
Press Shift Command Z, then Add Track > Video Track.

evaluate: Does an empty V1 read as somewhere to drop a clip before you have picked anything up?
Are the stripes quiet enough in light appearance, or do they need to be stronger?
With the drop ghost over part of the slot, do the two read as one idea?
Should a picked empty track (the blue wash on V2) still show its stripes, as it does now?
rough: Matches the mock's slot: dashed edge in the strong line colour, 45 degree stripes 6 points wide in the line colour at 60%, corner of 8.
The mock prints a sentence under the empty tracks ('A 1920 x 1080 timeline with no clips...'). It stays out, as it did on 2026-09-27: chrome may say a label of 30 characters at most (UX-PATTERNS §4).

While a file is held over a slot, the ghost covers only where the clip will land, its own length, and the rest of the lane keeps its stripes; the mock's step 3 lights the whole lane. The ghost's shape is from bring-in-a-second-clip-and-cut-between-clips, and this task (an-empty-track-looks-like-a-place-to-drop-a-clip) was asked to leave it unchanged.
A locked empty track keeps its locked stripes and no slot, and an empty Captions track has no slot, since neither takes a drop. No mock covers either.
